# Verse

> Offline Chinese speech-to-text for Windows, in Rust. A command-line tool and
> a desktop window over the same pipeline. Transcription runs locally with
> sherpa-onnx; nothing is uploaded, and the only network access in the program
> is `verse model fetch`.

Verse is designed to be driven by a program as well as by a person. Every
command takes `--json`; results go to stdout and diagnostics to stderr; failures
return distinct exit codes rather than a single non-zero.

## Commands

    verse transcribe <file|dir>... [options]
    verse model list [--json] [--models <dir>]
    verse model fetch <id> [--models <dir>]

A directory argument expands to the audio files beneath it, recursively,
sorted. One model is loaded for the whole batch — about 50× faster on a hundred
files than one process per file.

### transcribe options

    -o, --output <path>    output file, or directory when there are several inputs
        --format <srt|txt> srt (default) or txt
        --engine <id>      sensevoice (default) or qwen3-asr
        --models <dir>     model root, default `models`
        --vad <file>       voice-detector model
        --hotwords <terms> domain vocabulary; qwen3-asr only
        --hotwords-file <f> the same, read from a file
    -j, --jobs <n>         files at once, default 1; each worker loads its own model
        --json             one JSON document on stdout
        --fail-fast        stop at the first file that fails
    -o -                   write a single transcript to stdout

## Output contract

`--json` writes exactly one JSON document to stdout. Everything human-readable,
including progress and error messages, goes to stderr. Both single files and
batches produce the same shape, so a caller never branches on arity:

    {"version": 1, "engine": "sensevoice", "modelsDir": "models",
     "hotwords": null, "ok": true, "succeeded": 1, "failed": 0,
     "elapsedMs": 597, "warnings": [],
     "results": [{"input": "...", "output": "...", "format": "srt", "ok": true,
                  "elapsedMs": 597, "segmentCount": 1, "coverage": 0.998,
                  "recovered": false, "language": null, "text": "...",
                  "warnings": [], "segments": [{"startMs": 0, "endMs": 1500,
                  "text": "..."}], "error": null}]}

Every field is always present; `null` rather than absent. `version` describes
the document, not the tool. Timestamps are milliseconds; keys are camelCase.

`coverage` is the fraction of a file's non-silent audio that reached the
recogniser, and `recovered` is true when that fraction was implausible and the
file was recognised whole instead. **These two are how a caller judges whether
a transcript can be trusted**: a transcript that is short because the recording
was short and one that is short because audio was dropped are otherwise
identical.

`error.kind` is one of `io`, `network`, `decode`, `model`, `engine`, `sink`,
`registry`, `cancelled`, `internal` — the same vocabulary as the exit codes.

## Exit codes

    0  transcribed                 5  the recognition engine failed
    1  a bug                6  network
    2  the command line was wrong  7  cancelled
    3  the input was unreadable    8  the output could not be written
       or undecodable
    4  no usable model — run `verse model fetch <id>`

## Engines

| id | model | size | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sensevoice` | SenseVoice-Small int8 | 228 MB | default; fastest, smallest, best punctuation |
| `qwen3-asr` | Qwen3-ASR-0.6B int8 | 982 MB | most accurate on every domain measured; ~4× slower; the only one that takes `--hotwords` |

`--hotwords` gives a domain vocabulary, so a term is not substituted for a
homophone. It is passed through to sherpa-onnx unchanged; comma, full-width
comma, space and newline all delimit. Supplying it with an engine that cannot
use it warns on stderr and sets `hotwords` to `null` in the report — it never
passes silently.

Measured character error rate over 5049 utterances in five domains:
conversation 4.80%, meeting 6.95%, documentary 7.16%, phone call 8.42%, live
commerce 11.30%. Do not quote a single figure for this recogniser; the spread
is the finding.
